relevance_reason: Identifies a TBX22 splice mutation as the cause of X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome in the original family.

findings.statement: In a family with X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome of unknown cause, Pauws et al. (2013) found a novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) that segregated with the phenotype. In silico analysis predicted that the variant abolishes normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro splicing assay suggested that alternative splice sites were likely to be used. The authors concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
quotes: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.
All three variants were predicted to abolish normal mRNA splicing and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome.
most importantly confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations

findings.statement: Pauws et al. (2013) noted that the phenotype in the family with X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome goes beyond classic X-linked cleft palate (CPX) to include sensorineural deafness and coloboma. These features had not previously been reported in CPX patients but are consistent with the developmental expression pattern of Tbx22.
quotes: The phenotype extends to additional features including sensorineural deafness and coloboma, which are suggested by the Tbx22 developmental expression pattern but not previously associated in CPX patients.

findings.statement: Pauws et al. (2013) found a novel TBX22 splice donor variant (c.767+5G>A) and a previously known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G>A), both affecting the same exon as the Abruzzo-Erickson mutation, in patients with classic X-linked cleft palate. In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that both variants disrupt normal splicing.
quotes: A novel splice donor variant (c.767+5G>A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G>A) affecting the same exon were identified in patients with classic CPX phenotypes and were comparatively analyzed using both in silico and in vitro splicing studies.

relevance_reason: Describes the external ear anomalies of CHARGE syndrome, a related disorder. It is useful for comparison with the CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome but reports no patients with ABERS.

findings.statement: Davenport et al. (1986) described the external ear anomalies of CHARGE syndrome: short, wide pinnae that were often cupped and asymmetric; a distinctive triangular concha; a break between the antihelix and antitragus; and 'snipped-off' portions of the helical folds. The authors stated that these patterns were distinctive enough that a preliminary diagnosis of CHARGE syndrome could often be made from ear shape alone.
quotes: This paper describes the external ear anomalies found in this syndrome: short wide pinnae, often cupped and asymmetrical; distinctive triangular concha; discontinuity between the antihelix and antitragus; and 'snipped-off' portions of the helical folds.
The patterns of anomalies are so distinctive that a preliminary diagnosis of CHARGE Syndrome can often be made on the basis of ear shape alone.

relevance_reason: Case report of a mother and son with a familial CHARGE-like phenotype (coloboma, choanal atresia, cleft lip/palate, genital hypoplasia, short stature, hearing impairment), which bears on familial and X-linked CHARGE-like syndrome.

findings.statement: Metlay et al. (1987) reported a boy with CHARGE syndrome. He had a coloboma of the optic nerve head and a congenital heart defect (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect and parachute mitral valve). He also had choanal atresia, severe growth retardation, genital hypoplasia, abnormal ears, cleft lip and palate, and pectus carinatum. His chromosomes were normal, and he died at 19 months of age; autopsy findings were reported.
quotes: We report on a patient with CHARGE syndrome, as manifested by a coloboma of the optic nerve head, congenital heart defect (ASD, VSD, and parachute mitral valve), choanal atresia, severe growth retardation, genital hypoplasia, abnormal ears, cleft lip and palate, and pectus carinatum.
His chromosomes were normal. He died at 19 months.

phenotypes.text: coloboma of the optic nerve head

findings.statement: Metlay et al. (1987) noted that the mother of the affected boy was short and had hearing impairment, choanal atresia, and a coloboma. The authors suggested that this was evidence for dominant transmission of the disorder in this family, and they reviewed other familial cases from the literature.
quotes: His mother was short and had hearing impairment, choanal atresia, and a coloboma.
We suggest that this represents evidence for dominant transmission of this disorder in this family.

relevance_reason: Follow-up of the original family that defines Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome; the authors conclude the condition is not familial CHARGE syndrome.

findings.statement: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) did a follow-up study of the family they had previously reported with a new syndrome of cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis. The purpose was to assess how the patients had developed since then and to determine whether they had CHARGE syndrome.
quotes: Previously, we reported on a family with a new syndrome of cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis.
we decided to do a follow-up study on this family to assess the subsequent development of the patients and to determine if they have the CHARGE syndrome

findings.statement: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) noted that other reports had cited their family as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome. After the follow-up study, they concluded that the patients in this family did not have familial CHARGE syndrome or the CHARGE association.
quotes: This family has been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome.
We conclude that our patients do not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

relevance_reason: This is the original paper describing the syndrome that the entry is named after.

findings.statement: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) described a new syndrome characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis.
quotes: A new syndrome characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis has been described.

findings.statement: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) concluded that the family history suggested either autosomal dominant inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linked inheritance.
quotes: The family history suggests either an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.
